lines: Blank panel 1HP wide, for filling a gap in the rack
Blank panel 3HP wide, for filling a gap in the rack
Blank panel 5HP wide, for filling a gap in the rack
Buffered multiple copying one input to three outputs twice over, or one input to all six
Up copies IN A to the first three output jacks and IN B to the last three; down copies IN A to all six and leaves IN B unread
The signal copied to the first three output jacks, and to all six when the mode switch is down; a polyphonic cable keeps all its channels
The signal copied to the last three output jacks while the mode switch is up; with the switch down this jack is not read
A buffered copy of IN A, carrying the same number of polyphonic channels
A buffered copy of IN B while the mode switch is up, or of IN A when the switch is down
BufferedMult.notes: No port families given: a mult carries whatever is patched into it.

lines: Averaging mixer summing three inputs to one output twice over, or all six inputs to a single mix
Up keeps two groups, the IN A jacks averaged to the first output and the IN B jacks to the second; down averages all six inputs and sends that to both outputs
A signal averaged with the other patched IN A jacks, or with all six inputs when the mode switch is down
A signal averaged with the other patched IN B jacks, or with all six inputs when the mode switch is down
The sum of the patched IN A jacks divided by how many of them are patched, or the average of all six inputs when the mode switch is down
The sum of the patched IN B jacks divided by how many of them are patched, or the average of all six inputs when the mode switch is down
UnityMix.notes: No port families given: the module carries whatever is patched into it. An unpatched jack is left out of the average, so three patched jacks divide by three and one divides by one.

lines: Two-channel mixer with a fader and a direct out per channel, feeding either a stereo pair of mix outputs or the same mono mix on both
Sets the level of both mix outputs, silence fully left, 0dB at noon and +6dB fully right
Scales the level of the mix outputs, 0-10V for silence to the LEVEL setting, with voltage outside that range clamped; the CH direct outs are not affected
MONO sends the sum of both channels to both mix outputs; ST sends channel 1 to MX 1 and channel 2 to MX 2, and needs both input jacks patched or the mono sum is sent instead
Sets the level of the IN 1 signal, silence at the bottom and +6dB at the top, with 0dB at the default position
Sets the level of the IN 2 signal, silence at the bottom and +6dB at the top, with 0dB at the default position
The signal into channel 1; a polyphonic cable keeps all its channels
The signal into channel 2; a polyphonic cable keeps all its channels
Channel 1 after its fader, taken before the LEVEL knob and the CV input
Channel 2 after its fader, taken before the LEVEL knob and the CV input
In MONO the sum of both channels after their faders, the LEVEL knob and the CV; in ST the channel 1 signal alone
In MONO the sum of both channels after their faders, the LEVEL knob and the CV; in ST the channel 2 signal alone
Menu — Smooth level CV — adds a 6ms slew to the CV input, softening abrupt changes of level; it is ticked by default
Note — In ST both IN jacks must be patched for the mix outputs to be a stereo pair; with one of them empty the mono sum of both channels is sent to both outputs instead.
Two oscillators sweeping between square and saw, crossfaded to one output, with a separate sine wave following oscillator A
1V per octave for both oscillators and the sine, and the channel count here sets the module's polyphony; with OCT A at -1, 0V gives C4 at 261.63Hz
Fine-tunes both oscillators and the sine together, a tritone down at -2 and a tritone up at +2
Shifts oscillator A in whole octaves, -5 to 4, with -1 giving C4 for 0V at the V/OCT input
Shifts oscillator B in whole octaves, -5 to 4, with -1 giving C4 for 0V at the V/OCT input
Crossfades oscillator A between a square wave fully left and a saw wave fully right
Crossfades oscillator B between a square wave fully left and a saw wave fully right
Adds to the SHAPE A knob, a tenth of the crossfade per volt, clamped at square and at saw; only the first channel of a polyphonic cable is read
Adds to the SHAPE B knob, a tenth of the crossfade per volt, clamped at square and at saw; only the first channel of a polyphonic cable is read
Sets the pulse width of the square part of oscillator A, clamped between 1% and 99%; the saw part of the wave is unchanged
Sets the pulse width of the square part of oscillator B, clamped between 1% and 99%; the saw part of the wave is unchanged
Adds to the PW A knob, a tenth of the pulse width per volt, read per channel on a polyphonic cable
Adds to the PW B knob, a tenth of the pulse width per volt, read per channel on a polyphonic cable
Crossfades the OUT jack between oscillator A fully left and oscillator B fully right
Adds to the MIX knob, a tenth of the crossfade per volt, clamped at oscillator A alone and at oscillator B alone
Oscillator A and oscillator B crossfaded by MIX, -5V to 5V
A sine wave at the pitch of oscillator A, -5V to 5V, unchanged by SHAPE A, PW A and MIX
Horsehair.notes: The plugin description calls this a 3-oscillator VCO; the code runs two shape oscillators plus a sine taken from oscillator A. The README says 0V is middle C, which holds when an octave knob is at -1: the pitch fed to the oscillator is the knob value plus one, and the knobs come up at -2 for A and -1 for B. The two SHAPE CV inputs read channel one only, while the PW CV inputs are read per channel.

lines: Stereo mixer channel strip for the Daisy Mix chain, adding its signal to the running mix carried across touching modules
The left input, and the whole signal when the right input is unpatched, in which case it is copied to both sides before panning
The right input for this strip; leaving it unpatched sends the left input to both sides
Scales the level of this strip, 0-10V for silence to the fader setting, with voltage outside that range clamped
Sets the level of this strip, silence at the bottom and 0dB at the top, though the tooltip reads half the attenuation applied, so its -6dB is really -12dB
Pans this strip between left and right at constant power, centred at noon
Click to mute the strip, which lights red; hold the button for about a second to solo it instead, which lights green
The left side of this strip after the fader, the level CV and the pan, silent while the strip is muted unless the menu sets the direct outs pre-mute
The right side of this strip after the fader, the level CV and the pan, silent while the strip is muted unless the menu sets the direct outs pre-mute
Menu — Aux Group 1 Send Amt — a slider setting how much of this strip, taken after the fader, is passed down the chain to an AUX module set to group 1, 0% to 100%, and 0% until it is moved
Menu — Aux Group 2 Send Amt — a slider setting how much of this strip, taken after the fader, is passed down the chain to an AUX module set to group 2, 0% to 100%, and 0% until it is moved
Menu — Direct outs pre-mute — keeps the OUT jacks sounding while the strip is muted, so the strip can be processed elsewhere without its dry signal in the mix
Menu — Smooth level CV — adds a 6ms slew to the level CV input, softening abrupt changes of level; it is ticked by default
Note — A strip takes the running mix from the daisy module touching its left edge and passes that mix plus its own signal to the one touching its right edge, ending at a D-MX2 master
Note — The two lamps in the blue DAISY band light when a daisy module is linked on the left and on the right, and the red number shows this strip's place in the chain
Note — When a strip anywhere in the chain is soloed, the master carries only the soloed strips
Note — With the mouse over this module, pressing m toggles mute and pressing s toggles solo
Note — Up to 16 strips can feed one master
Note — The strip adds nothing to any mix on its own: it needs a D-MX2 master at the right-hand end of an unbroken run of touching daisy modules.
DaisyChannel2.notes: The fader's tooltip reads half the attenuation the code applies: the displayed dB is 20 times the log of the knob value while the gain applied is that value squared, so a tooltip of -6dB is really -12dB. The README says the solo hold is 1.5 seconds; the code counts 50 drag frames, which is nearer a second at 60 frames per second. Each strip's contribution is divided by 16 for the chain and multiplied by 16 again at the master.

lines: Stereo meter for the Daisy Mix chain, showing the signal of the daisy module touching its left edge and passing the running mix on to the right
Note — Each ladder reads from -60dB in steps of 1.5dB, green to -13.5dB, yellow to -1.5dB, and red for the top four steps ending at 4.5dB
Note — Placed against a DC2 strip it shows that strip's own signal, against an AUX it shows that aux group's collected sends, and against a D-MX2 it shows the master mix
Note — The two lamps in the blue DAISY band light when a daisy module is linked on the left and on the right
Note — The ladders stay dark unless a daisy module touches the left edge; the meter reads nothing of its own.
Aux send bus for the Daisy Mix chain, collecting the send amounts set on the DC2 strips earlier in the chain and offering them as a stereo pair
Each press switches this module between aux group 1 and aux group 2, shown by the two blue lamps, and it then collects the sends set to that group
The left side of the collected sends from the DC2 strips earlier in the chain that carry a send amount for the selected group
The right side of the collected sends from the DC2 strips earlier in the chain that carry a send amount for the selected group
Note — This module takes the running mix from the daisy module touching its left edge and passes it unchanged to the one touching its right edge, adding nothing of its own to the mix
Note — Bringing processed aux signal back into the mix takes a further DC2 strip placed later in the chain as a return
Note — The two lamps in the blue DAISY band light when a daisy module is linked on the left and on the right
Note — The two outputs are silent until a DC2 strip earlier in the chain has its Aux Group 1 or Aux Group 2 Send Amt raised on that strip's right-click menu; every strip starts at 0%.
Blank separator 2HP wide for the Daisy Mix chain, passing the running mix and both aux buses from the daisy module touching its left edge to the one touching its right
Note — The two lamps in the blue DAISY band light when a daisy module is linked on the left and on the right
Master bus for a Daisy Mix chain, summing the strips linked to its left into a stereo output
Sets the level of the mix, silence fully left, 0dB at noon and +6dB fully right
Scales the mix level, 0-10V for silence to the MASTER setting, with voltage outside that range clamped
Mutes the master bus and lights red, despite the README describing a long-press solo on this button
The left side of the chain mix, clamped to -12V to 12V before the MASTER knob and the level CV are applied, despite the README putting that clamp on the output
The right side of the chain mix, clamped to -12V to 12V before the MASTER knob and the level CV are applied, despite the README putting that clamp on the output
Menu — Smooth level CV — adds a 6ms slew to the level CV input, softening abrupt changes of level; it is ticked by default
Menu — Create 1 channel — places one DC2 strip to the left of the master, touching it, so it is linked into the chain
Menu — Create 1 channel with vu meter — places one DC2 strip to the left of the master with a VU meter module beside it
Menu — Create 2 channels — places two DC2 strips to the left of the master, touching it and each other
Menu — Create 2 channels with vu meters — places two DC2 strips to the left of the master, each with a VU meter module beside it
Menu — Create 2 channels with vu meters + aux sends — places two DC2 strips with meters, then a blank separator, two AUX modules and two more DC2 strips with meters to bring the aux signal back
Menu — Create 4 channels — places four DC2 strips to the left of the master, touching it and each other
Menu — Create 4 channels with vu meters — places four DC2 strips to the left of the master, each with a VU meter module beside it
Menu — Create 4 channels with vu meters + aux sends — places four DC2 strips with meters, then a blank separator, two AUX modules and two more DC2 strips with meters to bring the aux signal back
Note — The master takes the mix from the daisy module touching its left edge, so it goes at the right-hand end of the chain, and up to 16 strips can feed it
Note — When a strip anywhere in the chain is soloed, only the soloed strips reach the outputs
Note — With the mouse over this module, pressing m toggles mute
Note — The outputs carry nothing until at least one DC2 strip touches the chain to the left; the master has no input jacks of its own.
DaisyMaster2.notes: The README gives this module a mute button with a long-press solo turning green; the code configures a plain two-state mute with a red lamp, and the long-press solo belongs to the DC2 strip. The README also says the master clamps its output to 12V: the clamp is applied to the chain sum before the level knob, so a knob above 0dB takes the output past 12V. While muted the output jacks are left unwritten rather than zeroed, so they hold their last voltage.

The signal into this strip, taken through the fader and the level CV
